text:
maria: Seeing a weird canary spike — ~0.8% of SSE sessions get routed to `eu-low` during quota fallthrough, then drop within 4s. Console shows the request as successful and no route change. logs: `session=sh_9f3 route=eu-low fallthrough=true route_chain=[us-high->eu-low] auth_err=none disconnect=early`
kevin: do you have a trace id or sample event? can you paste the upstream proxy logs? :eyes:
maria: paste below (sanitized):
```
> 2025-11-02T21:14:03Z proxy-01 INF handleRequest req_id=tx-9a7 route=us-high -> fallthrough -> eu-low final_route=eu-low session_id=sh_9f3 resume_token=rt_33c latency_ms=4100
> 2025-11-02T21:14:03Z proxy-01 DBG sendResume header=X-Route-Chain:us-high,eu-low
> 2025-11-02T21:14:03Z backend-eu-low INF acceptSession session=sh_9f3 auth_ok=true
> 2025-11-02T21:14:07Z backend-eu-low WARN unexpected EOF session=sh_9f3
```
kevin: hmm `sendResume` includes X-Route-Chain but our public console traces do not show it — that's why ops couldn't see the handoff. also suspect ticketing: quota attributed to us-high but session charged on eu-low causing billing mismatch.
jess: agreed — console UX needs quick visibility: add `route_chain` and `final_route_tier` to the per-session trace and make them filterable. also add a compact pill for "fell back" with hover explaining why (quota, capacity, auth).
alex: root cause framing: current fallthrough policy prefers "cheapest compatible" route (eu-low) when capacity is exhausted, even if it changes region. that avoids latency SLO but breaks session affinity + different auth domains. proposal: change order to prefer same-region fallback with spare capacity > cross-region low-tier. fallback policy PR: `prefer(same_region, spare_capacity) -> prefer(low_cost)`
kevin: telemetry ask: we should emit `route_handoff` event with fields [orig_route, target_route, reason, sampling_rate] and a `session_rehome` counter per tenant. console dashboard panel: stacked bar of handoffs by reason (quota/capacity/auth).
sre-bot: ALERT 7532109999: sse_reconnect_spike detected (rate +420%) — affected routes: eu-low (peak 03:21 UTC) — linked traces: tx-9a7, tx-9b2, tx-9c1
jess: for short-term mitigation can we make proxy include `X-Final-Route` in the SSE handshake and include `route_chain` in the session metadata payload? that way consumer apps and console can attribute immediately.
maria: verified quick patch locally: `proxy: set header X-Final-Route=${final_route}` on accept, and add `session.meta.route_chain` to session create event. test looks good — no auth mismatch in my run.
alex: deploy plan: canary 10% with routing-policy toggle OFF to avoid cross-region fallthrough for 6h. If stable, flip for 50% then global. update runbook to include rollback if resume failures >0.1%/min.
kevin: will open telemetry PR + dashboard tile. also adding `route_handoff` into the existing span so traces link to it.
jess: small console UX ask: add an operator column showing `route_chain` with hover breadcrumbs and a quick "jump to final route metrics" button. UX team already has a slot next week.
maria: leaving a snippet command to reproduce a handoff locally: `curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TEST" -H "X-Debug-Trace: 1" "https://api.redwood-inference.internal/sse?model=canary&region=us-west"` you should see `X-Route-Chain` in the proxy debug logs and `X-Final-Route` in response headers.
sre-bot: NOTE: added incident link -> https://redwood.internal/incidents/INC-2025-789 (ops runbook updated) :+1:
kevin: filing the proxy PR now (will include tests for header population and an e2e that asserts `route_chain` appears in console traces). tagging @jess for UX changes.
jess: thanks — will shepherd the console change. :thumbsup:
maria: thanks all, will monitor canary after deploy tilt. if anyone sees new handoffs ping me.
